description: Blood Relations is an important part of Verbal Reasoning. It involves analyzing the relationships between family members to find an unknown relation based on the given information.

sections.title: Basic Family Relationships
sections.description: It is essential to understand the relationships on both the paternal and maternal sides of the family.

key_concepts.explanation: Relations from the father's side, such as Uncle, Aunt, Grandfather, and Grandmother.
Relations from the mother's side, such as Maternal Uncle, Maternal Aunt, Maternal Grandfather, and Maternal Grandmother.
Children of the same parents, such as a brother and a sister.
Relationships formed through marriage, such as Mother-in-law, Father-in-law, and Brother-in-law.

sections.title: Family Tree and Symbols
sections.description: Drawing a Family Tree is the most effective way to easily solve these questions.

key_concepts.explanation: A square or a plus sign (+) is used to represent a male, while a circle or a minus sign (-) is used for a female.
A double arrow or an equal to sign is used to represent the relationship between a husband and a wife.
A horizontal line is used to represent siblings or cousins.
A vertical line is used to represent the generation gap between parents and children.

sections.title: Types of Blood Relation Questions
sections.description: There are mainly three types of Blood Relation questions asked in exams.

results: A person points to another person or a photograph and explains the relationship.
To solve this, place yourself in the speaker's position or trace the relationship in reverse order.
Relationships are represented by special symbols like A @ B, A $ B.
You must decode the equation by understanding the meaning of each symbol to find the relationship.
Information about multiple family members and their professions is given together.
It is solved by drawing a complete family tree.

sections.title: Steps to Solve
sections.description: A step-by-step method to solve any Blood Relation question accurately.

steps.title: Break down the information
steps.detail: Instead of reading the whole question at once, break it into smaller sentences or segments.

steps.title: Draw Family Tree
steps.detail: Based on the given data, draw a generation-by-generation diagram using appropriate symbols.

steps.title: Determine Gender
steps.detail: Mark the gender only when there is clear information. Do not guess the gender based solely on a name.

steps.title: Find Final Relation
steps.detail: Read carefully at the end of the question from whose perspective the relation is asked. Example: 'How is A related to B?' means you have to tell 'Who is A to B'.

sections.title: Important Cases to Remember
sections.description: It is essential to keep certain conditions in mind to avoid common mistakes.

results: Do not determine gender based only on a name (like Sonu, Kiran, Kamal) unless explicitly stated as 'Son', 'Daughter', 'Husband', or 'Wife'.
'Only Son' means there is no other son in the family, but there can be daughters.
'Only Child' means the person has no other siblings.
Always note from which person the relation is being asked. If the answer is 'Uncle', the options might also have 'Nephew', so identify the correct direction of the relationship.
